prompt: In `memory.py`, who decides whether a proposed memory is kept?

choices.text: The model, when it chooses the kind
choices.why: The kind sets the retention; whether to keep is decided after.

choices.text: The client, who approves every memory
choices.why: Nobody is asked; the client can see and delete afterwards.

choices.text: The provider, under its retention terms
choices.why: The provider never sees the store.

choices.text: The code, with rules the model cannot change
choices.why: Right: the model proposes; the code decides.

prompt: Which proposals did the code refuse? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the CPF for the invoice
choices.why: Yes: `detect.py` found it.

choices.text: the new phone number
choices.why: Yes: `detect.py` found it.

choices.text: the stay in hospital for a surgery
choices.why: Yes: the sensitive list found the health words.

choices.text: the client's name
choices.why: Yes: kind `contact` is not kept.

choices.text: the dark blue logo
choices.why: It was kept, as a preference.

choices.text: the weekly updates
choices.why: It was kept, as a preference.

prompt: Why is a memory of kind `contact` refused even when it holds no number?
hint: Where else does that fact live?

choices.text: It lives in the account record, where the client edits it
choices.why: Right: a second copy goes stale the day the client changes it.

choices.text: Names are sensitive data under the LGPD
choices.why: A name is personal data, not one of the sensitive kinds.

choices.text: The schema does not allow the kind `contact`
choices.why: The schema allows it; the code refuses it.

choices.text: The model cannot spell names reliably
choices.why: Spelling is not the reason.

prompt: The model proposes a preference: "her daughter's school is in Moema". What do the rules in `memory.py` do with it?

choices.text: `detect.py` refuses it as personal data
choices.why: It has no CPF, card, phone, e-mail or key in it.

choices.text: The sensitive list refuses it as health data
choices.why: None of its words is on the list.

choices.text: It is kept, because no rule sees it
choices.why: Right: a list of refused things is never complete, which is why scope and expiry matter.

choices.text: The schema refuses it for being too long
choices.why: It is well under 120 characters.

prompt: How many memories did the code keep from the three messages?
Why does `show --as ac-0Z5Q` list no memories?

choices.text: Its memories have all expired
choices.why: It never had any.

choices.text: Each account reads only its own file
choices.why: Right: the store is partitioned by account before anything is looked up.

choices.text: The sweep deleted them on 21 March
choices.why: The sweep ran on 1 July, and only for expired lines.

choices.text: Its client asked for them to be forgotten
choices.why: Nothing was ever kept for that account.

prompt: On 1 July, before the sweep, how many lines did `data/memory/ac-7Q2M.jsonl` still hold?
`show` already hides expired memories. Why is `sweep` still needed?
hint: What does the LGPD ask about?

choices.text: `show` is too slow on large files
choices.why: Speed is not the argument.

choices.text: Expired lines confuse the model's ranking
choices.why: The model never sees expired lines; `show` hides them.

choices.text: `sweep` refreshes the dates of the useful memories
choices.why: It only deletes; it never extends a date.

choices.text: Data on disk is held, whether used or not
choices.why: Right: the question is what Tarefa holds.

prompt: The lesson's warning: a memory with no expiry date is kept for ___ by default.
"Always pays by Pix" was filed as `job`, kept 90 days, not as `preference`, kept 365. Why does the lesson accept this error more easily than the opposite one?
hint: Which way does it move the date?

choices.text: It shortens how long the fact is kept
choices.why: Right: an error that shortens a memory is the safe direction.

choices.text: Payment facts are never personal data
choices.why: How somebody pays is about them.

choices.text: The client will correct it in the next chat
choices.why: Nothing asks the client about the kind.

choices.text: Ninety days and a year are the same to the LGPD
choices.why: The law asks for no longer than needed; the two are not the same.

prompt: What does `guard memory forget m4` do the second time it is run?
hint: Look at the last command of the capture.

choices.text: It prints that m4 was forgotten again
choices.why: That would claim a deletion that did not happen.

choices.text: It deletes the next memory instead
choices.why: It deletes only the id it was given.

choices.text: It prints an error and exits with 1
choices.why: Right: a screen that says forgotten whatever happened is a screen that lies.

choices.text: It restores m4 from the conversation
choices.why: Nothing is rebuilt; the id is simply absent.

prompt: Which copies does deleting a memory line not reach? Choose all that apply.
hint: Where else did the text go?

choices.text: the conversation in the call log
choices.why: Yes: it lives under the log's own retention, lesson 11.

choices.text: prompts already sent to the provider
choices.why: Yes: the provider keeps them under its terms, lesson 12.

choices.text: a summary of the client written for staff
choices.why: Yes: anything derived from the memory is a copy.

choices.text: the line in `data/memory/ACCOUNT.jsonl`
choices.why: That is exactly what `forget` deletes.

choices.text: what `show` lists afterwards
choices.why: `show` reads the file, so the line is gone from it.

prompt: Why does the lesson treat a recalled memory as client text?
hint: Where did its words come from?

choices.text: It is stored outside Tarefa's servers
choices.why: The store is on Tarefa's servers.

choices.text: It came from the client's messages, through the model
choices.why: Right: lesson 13's second lens follows the text, not the server.

choices.text: Clients can edit their memories directly
choices.why: They can see and delete; they do not write lines.

choices.text: It is written in the client's language
choices.why: Language is not what makes text untrusted.

prompt: Match each kind of memory to what `memory.py` does with it.
hint: One answer on the right is no kind's.

prompt: Put the life of one memory in order.
hint: From a message to the disk and off it.
items: The model proposes a memory in a closed shape
The code checks it against its rules
It is kept with a date in the client's own file
The sweep deletes it after that date

prompt: "The model proposes; the code decides" was first the rule for which part of Tarefa's assistant?

choices.text: The filter chain of lesson 5
choices.why: Filters check replies; they do not decide on proposals.

choices.text: The input checks of lesson 9
choices.why: Those check what goes in, not what the model proposes.

choices.text: The minimisation of lesson 12
choices.why: That decides what reaches the provider.

choices.text: The tool gate of lesson 10
choices.why: Right: tool calls first, memories now.

prompt: After `forget m4`, how many memories does `ac-7Q2M` have in use on 1 July?
hint: The second `show` in the last capture.

prompt: Tarefa plans to keep every client's memories in one shared vector index and look them up by similarity. What does the lesson require of that design?
hint: Lesson 15 had the same problem with documents.

choices.text: Nothing, as long as each line keeps its date
choices.why: A date limits how long, not whose.

choices.text: A sentence in the prompt naming the client
choices.why: Lessons 14 and 15 showed a sentence is a request.

choices.text: Partition by the account before any lookup
choices.why: Right: the account from the session, applied before similarity.

choices.text: Shorter memories, so they match less often
choices.why: Length does not change whose memory comes back.
